questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Regions in the Plane Where a Function Is Positive or Negative
questions.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x-1)(y-2).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)>0?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=1$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have a strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/2ae1b749a56deaef05254ff376acbd44885337b06b49473cb9b19b4fa57f6c84.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/6434bee1a3dc38292675749072f046d4af6239ce6a8f71f102a9b29637679da4.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-1)$ | $(y-2)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(0,3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(2,3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(0,1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(2,1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)>0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/17551c745895bac085fc289f9ff0f26531bc518891815e252885fd75d81a0af0.png)

questions.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=(x+1)(2-y).$ What are the missing entries in the sign table of $f(x,y),$ shown below?

| $y>2$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ |  |  |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-1$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/d5d7c89d619aa13d7fea8bc1260a08cb8678fb260e4431508c5f4c8c53e7ba5e.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/6cce64627f21f6cc17efc789614a0bd582ded827a0938f01c9b756e0cb461862.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+1)$ | $(2-y)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-2,3)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(0,3)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(0,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/c24cc3ab0812bfae6834ff8c3a68668c3925f6e39e29a453ea6bc27fbc9f6c74.png)

Finally, we fill in the table as follows:

| $y>2$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<2$ | $-$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |

questions.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+2){y}^{3}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-2$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/975b596621dab7d455b09d75b1c8d2b9fd73e75cd2169ec40aadda48673f6883.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/9466a3fbf682ce967cda2294cfb61d5fa40b4f7c91686cfc8653cb4c1ffb4e97.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+2)$ | ${y}^{3}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-3,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(-1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-3,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(-1,-1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\ge 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/b8e5807115c13aa842364a174058d1081bd84eba10dce13390da93832a1aeb54.png)
